verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 6.6
verses.english: Linked Discourses 6.6

verses.pali: 1. Paṭhamavagga
verses.english: 1. The Appeal

verses.pali: Brahmalokasutta
verses.english: The Negligent Divinity

verses.pali: Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
verses.english: At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno.
verses.english: Now at that time the Buddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

verses.pali: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṁ dvārabāhaṁ upanissāya aṭṭhaṁsu. Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā suddhāvāsaṁ paccekabrahmānaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa went to the Buddha and stationed themselves one by each door-post. But Subrahmā said to Suddhāvāsa,

verses.pali: “akālo kho tāva, mārisa, bhagavantaṁ payirupāsituṁ;
verses.english: “Good fellow, it’s the wrong time to pay homage to the Buddha.

verses.pali: divāvihāragato bhagavā paṭisallīno ca.
verses.english: He has gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

verses.pali: Asuko ca brahmaloko iddho ceva phīto ca, brahmā ca tatra pamādavihāraṁ viharati.
verses.english: But such and such realm of divinity is successful and prosperous, while the divinity living there is negligent.

verses.pali: Āyāma, mārisa, yena so brahmaloko tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ brahmānaṁ saṁvejeyyāmā”ti.
verses.english: Come, let’s go to that realm of divinity and inspire awe in that Divinity!”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, mārisā”ti kho suddhāvāso paccekabrahmā subrahmuno paccekabrahmuno paccassosi.
verses.english: “Yes, good fellow,” replied Suddhāvāsa.

verses.pali: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso …pe… evameva—bhagavato purato antarahitā tasmiṁ brahmaloke pāturahesuṁ.
verses.english: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, they vanished from in front of the Buddha and appeared in that realm of divinity.

verses.pali: Addasā kho so brahmā te brahmāno dūratova āgacchante. Disvāna te brahmāno etadavoca:
verses.english: That divinity saw those divinities coming off in the distance and said to them,

verses.pali: “handa kuto nu tumhe, mārisā, āgacchathā”ti?
verses.english: “Well now, good fellows, where have you come from?”

verses.pali: “Āgatā kho mayaṁ, mārisa, amha tassa bhagavato santikā arahato sammāsambuddhassa.
verses.english: “Good fellow, we’ve come from the presence of the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.

verses.pali: Gaccheyyāsi pana tvaṁ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti?
verses.english: Shouldn’t you go to attend on that Blessed One?”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutto, kho so brahmā taṁ vacanaṁ anadhivāsento sahassakkhattuṁ attānaṁ abhinimminitvā subrahmānaṁ paccekabrahmānaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When they had spoken, that divinity refused to accept their advice. He multiplied himself a thousand times and said to Subrahmā,

verses.pali: “passasi me no tvaṁ, mārisa, evarūpaṁ iddhānubhāvan”ti?
verses.english: “Good fellow, can’t you see that I have such psychic power?”

verses.pali: “Passāmi kho tyāhaṁ, mārisa, evarūpaṁ iddhānubhāvan”ti.
verses.english: “I see that, good fellow.”

verses.pali: “So khvāhaṁ, mārisa, evaṁmahiddhiko evaṁmahānubhāvo kassa aññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā upaṭṭhānaṁ gamissāmī”ti?
verses.english: “Since I have such psychic power and might, what other ascetic or brahmin should I go to and attend upon?”

verses.pali: Atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā dvisahassakkhattuṁ attānaṁ abhinimminitvā taṁ brahmānaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Subrahmā multiplied himself two thousand times and said to that Divinity,

verses.pali: “passasi me no tvaṁ, mārisa, evarūpaṁ iddhānubhāvan”ti?
verses.english: “Good fellow, can’t you see that I have such psychic power?”

verses.pali: “Passāmi kho tyāhaṁ, mārisa, evarūpaṁ iddhānubhāvan”ti.
verses.english: “I see that, good fellow.”

verses.pali: “Tayā ca kho, mārisa, mayā ca sveva bhagavā mahiddhikataro ceva mahānubhāvataro ca.
verses.english: “That Buddha has even more psychic power and might than you or me.

verses.pali: Gaccheyyāsi tvaṁ, mārisa, tassa bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassā”ti?
verses.english: Shouldn’t you go to attend on that Blessed One?”

verses.pali: Atha kho so brahmā subrahmānaṁ paccekabrahmānaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
verses.english: Then that divinity addressed Subrahmā in verse:

verses.pali: “Tayo supaṇṇā caturo ca haṁsā,
verses.english: “There are three hundreds of phoenixes, four of swans,

verses.pali: Byagghīnisā pañcasatā ca jhāyino;
verses.english: and five of tigerhawks. To he who practiced absorption

verses.pali: Tayidaṁ vimānaṁ jalate ca brahme,
verses.english: belongs this palace; it shines, Divinity,

verses.pali: Obhāsayaṁ uttarassaṁ disāyan”ti.
verses.english: lighting up the northern quarter!”

verses.pali: “Kiñcāpi te taṁ jalate vimānaṁ,
verses.english: “So what if your palace shines,

verses.pali: Obhāsayaṁ uttarassaṁ disāyaṁ;
verses.english: lighting up the northern quarter?

verses.pali: Rūpe raṇaṁ disvā sadā pavedhitaṁ,
verses.english: A clever person, seeing the strife in form,

verses.pali: Tasmā na rūpe ramatī sumedho”ti.
verses.english: its chronic trembling, takes no pleasure in it.”

verses.pali: Atha kho subrahmā ca paccekabrahmā suddhāvāso ca paccekabrahmā taṁ brahmānaṁ saṁvejetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṁsu.
verses.english: Then after inspiring awe in that divinity, the independent divinities Subrahmā and Suddhāvāsa vanished right there.

verses.pali: Agamāsi ca kho so brahmā aparena samayena bhagavato upaṭṭhānaṁ arahato sammāsambuddhassāti.
verses.english: And after some time that divinity went to attend on the Buddha.
